#44 THE CRIMSON SKIES `Tr` ROW, COMPLETED FOR ALL THREE MODES.

WHY THIS EXISTS, and it is a correction rather than a new question. [issue.44]'s strongest accuracy claim reads 'THE BOUND CLOSES THE RACE ON A REAL TITLE: Crimson Skies Tr goes 0.6172/0.6188 to EXACTLY 0 over 13,751 uploads'. Tracing each number to the run that produced it: 11,829/19,167 and 11,866/19,176 are 1789312621-draw-only-crimson-1052969 and -1053039 at ref 5cfc236d9b, which is MODE 0; 0/13,751 and 0/13,901 are -1053164 and 1789312622-...-1053270 at ref d879e6e03b, which is MODE 2. **Mode 1 has never been run on Crimson Skies at all** -- zero requests name both that title and a mode-1 ref, and the two mode-1 Galleon logs carry no `Tr:` line at any point because the probe did not exist at that ref. So the issue credits mode 1 with mode 2's only real-title accuracy evidence, and the decision has been framed for two days as 'mode 1 correct and expensive, mode 2 cheap and unproven' on the strength of it.

This sweep measures the cell that was never measured, and re-measures the other two at a tip-based ref on the live device, so the row stops resting on the offline nova at ~530 commits behind.

WHY THESE REFS AND NOT ONE BINARY. `Tr` needs -DHAKUX_VRAM_RACE_PROBE=1; the tip defaults that probe to 0 (vk/draw.c:65) so a stock build appends nothing to the pacing line. And HAKUX_FIFO_SKEW_BOUND cannot reach the emulator through the queue: the app reads its environment from the `env_vars` pref in x1box_prefs.xml and no dispatch script writes that pref. So each mode is a ref -- three children of one probe-on base, differing from each other by one line of pfifo.c, each carrying its own apk_sha.

PROBE-ON RUNS ARE COMPARABLE ONLY WITH PROBE-ON RUNS. The probe is an RCU read plus a dirty-bitmap scan on two per-draw paths, which is why it is defaulted off. No `gfps` figure from this sweep may be compared with one from a stock build, and none is registered below. The cost half of #44 is measured by the separate stock-build Galleon sweep.

T0 (VALIDITY GATE on the mode-0 arm ALONE; the sweep is VOID, not passed, if it fails): mode 0 shows Tr/tex_uploads >= 0.40 in both runs. The 2026-09-13 baseline is 0.6172 and 0.6188, reproducible to 0.26%, and a separate reading at a different ref gave 0.617. A zero or near-zero control would mean the race had been closed by something else between then and now, at which point T1 and T2 are passed by luck and prove nothing. This is the leg that stops the 'stale floor turned the falsifier into a coin flip' failure, and it is the one this issue's OTHER observable already died of: stale_px on the Texture border disc reads 0 of 10 non-zero at the tip, so a no-fix binary passes its bar with probability ~1.

T1 (THE NEVER-MEASURED CELL): mode 1 shows Tr = exactly 0 in both runs. Registered as exact zero and not 'smaller' for the reason [issue.44] already gives: against a baseline reproducible to 0.26% a timing perturbation would MOVE the rate, not annihilate it. FAILS on any non-zero Tr. A failure here would be the interesting outcome -- mode 1 is the STRONGER bound, so a non-zero Tr under mode 1 with a zero under mode 2 would mean the two modes are not ordered the way the guarantee says they are, and that is a fact about the implementation rather than about the workload.

T2 (THE STALENESS CLOSURE): mode 2 shows Tr = exactly 0 in both runs, reproducing 0/13,751 and 0/13,901 at a tip-based ref on a different device. FAILS on any non-zero Tr.

T3 (THE IMPOSSIBLE ROW, an internal control): Xd = 0 on every run of every arm. Xd counts a range that read dirty and then read clean on an immediate re-check, which cannot happen if the probe's page arithmetic and RCU read are right. A non-zero Xd indicts the instrument and VOIDS the whole sweep rather than reporting a defect. Every run on disk reads Xd = 0, so this is a control with a known value and not a hope.

T4 (DID MODE 1 EXECUTE -- direct counter): the `fifoskew` line on the mode-1 arm reads bound=1 and held(n)/kicks >= 0.90. Mode 1 read 1.0000 on Galleon.

T5 (DID MODE 2 EXECUTE, AND NOT BY BAILING): the `fifoskew` line on the mode-2 arm reads bound=2, scan(n) > 0, and big/scan_n < 0.01. Deliberately NOT held(n)/kicks, which on Crimson read 0.7026 for a mode 2 that was working perfectly -- a 0.90 bar would manufacture a failure. The bail counter is the leg because a scan reaching FIFO_SKEW_SCAN_MAX_WORDS falls through to mode 1's path, and held(n)/kicks reads as an intact guarantee under both stories.

TENSION, so that no inert arm passes: T0 and T1/T2 cannot both be satisfied by a binary that does nothing -- a no-op fails T1/T2, and a binary that somehow zeroed Tr by disabling texture uploads would take tex_uploads to 0 and fail T0's denominator on the control arm. T4/T5 cannot be satisfied by turning the bound off. And T1 failing while T2 passes is a named world with a named consequence, not an unexplained outcome.
